verdict.headline: Iran launches surprise attack; hawkish Fed and META collapse convert the market to BEARISH
verdict.label: BEARISH conversion — SPX 7,316 below 7,380 threshold; Iran IRGC missiles on US Jordan base shattered ceasefire and sent Brent +7.9% to $90.74; FOMC 9-3 hawkish hold drove 30Y to 5.193% (highest since 2007); META Q2 EPS $6.18 missed $7.18 est with 31% operating margin (from 43%); MSFT Azure 43% beat provides Thursday morning offset (AH +7.57%)
verdict.rationale_short: The session delivered a triple shock: Iran's Revolutionary Guard launched ballistic missiles at US forces in Jordan, shattering the mutual pause that had briefly cleared Brent below $85 on Tuesday; the FOMC voted 9-3 with three members preferring an immediate hike, driving the 30-year yield to 5.193% — its highest since 2007; and META's operating margin collapsed 12 points to 31% as Q2 AI capex reached $31 billion, with EPS missing by $1.00 per share. The S&P 500 closed at 7,316, below the 7,380 BEARISH threshold for the first time in this regime framework. MSFT Azure at 43% growth (a beat of the critical 42% threshold) and the resulting AH rally (+7.57%) provide Thursday's open-side offset, but the directional lean entering tomorrow is bearish until Iran, 30-year yields at 18-year highs, and the META AI capex ROI pattern resolve.

dont_buy.ticker: META at or near AH levels ($529)
dont_buy.reason: META's Q2 2026 result represents a structural regime change in its AI investment thesis: operating margin at 31% versus 43% a year ago means the AI infrastructure buildout is materially destroying per-share earnings even as revenue grows 28%. Q2 capex alone was $31.08 billion — more in one quarter than many companies spend in a year. EPS declined 13% year-over-year despite double-digit revenue growth. The forward guidance ($61–64B Q3 revenue) implies mid-to-high 20s percent growth, which is a deceleration from Q2's 28% and does not address the margin path. Buying the AH dip at $529 is catching a falling knife in a name with no operating leverage pathway established.
dont_buy.better_entry: Post-Q3 2026 AH (October earnings): entry is defensible only if META shows operating margin recovery toward 38–40% and capex moderates. The earliest re-entry condition is Q3 2026 showing capex below $28B in the quarter AND operating margin re-expansion above 36%.

MSFT Azure 43% is a counterweight, but META's result today is the dominant negative signal for the sector's narrative. NVDA circular financing + META margin collapse + oil at $90 is not a setup to build a sector position.
dont_buy.better_entry: Post-AAPL/AMZN Thursday AH and post-PCE Friday close. If AAPL China iPhone units beat AND AMZN AWS confirms AI inference demand growth AND PCE does not re-accelerate above 3.5%, the AI demand narrative reconstruction is underway and SMH re-entry with stop at Tuesday's close becomes defensible.

trade_setups.thesis: Azure 43% constant currency growth (beat the critical 42% threshold) is the most important AI demand confirmation of the Q2 earnings cycle so far. MSFT reported $90.01B in revenue (+18%), beat EPS ($4.74 vs $4.24), and confirmed AI ARR at $37B+ (+123% YoY). This is not a marginal beat — it is a definitive demonstration that AI cloud demand is organic, not circular-loan-driven, and that hyperscaler AI investment is generating real incremental revenue. The market priced a 7.57% after-hours rally. Thursday's gap open is the setup: buy the open toward $415–420 with a hard stop at the regular-session close of $390.54.

The fundamental thesis: META's AI capex cycle is destroying per-share earnings with no stated inflection point or operating leverage milestone. Free cash flow is dwindling. Q3 guidance ($61–64B) implies deceleration from Q2's 28% without any margin recovery path indicated.

bear_case: Counter-argument: The evening's most important data point is MSFT Azure at 43% constant currency growth — the definitive refutation of the circular financing thesis. If the AI demand driving Azure's 43% growth is real (and Azure's external customer base is not NVDA-funded), then the concern that AI infrastructure investment is circular and unsustainable is overstated. Iran's missile attack on Jordan was fully intercepted by US forces with no casualties reported, and Trump's 'hit them hard' language is consistent with past posturing that did not produce open military escalation. The ceasefire framework can be quickly reinstated if both parties return to the Oman channel. META's margin collapse, while severe, is a company-specific capital allocation decision — not a demand signal that AI infrastructure spending is about to contract. Tomorrow's catalysts (AAPL Q2, AMZN AWS, Q2 GDP) could all surprise positively, and MSFT's +7.57% AH gap is a real morning lift for the technology sector. If SPX reclaims 7,380 on Thursday's close, AND AAPL beats China iPhone consensus AND AMZN AWS confirms AI inference demand above 30%, the BEARISH conversion is a single-session false signal.
